# Agent: artifact-author

> **Model:** `sonnet` | **Tools:** Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
> **Role:** Skill & Instructions Author — converts validated research into operational artifacts (SKILL.md, subagents, and rules/instructions) ready for use by agents.

**What it does:** Reads a research document generated by `framework-researcher`, applies the authoring standards integrated into the `skill-creator` (three-tier, progressive disclosure, correct YAML) and produces one or more skill or instruction files.

**What it does NOT do:** Research technologies on the web, audit architecture, validate quality of existing artifacts.

**Universal prerequisite:** The research document (`research_<Tech>_v<Version>.md`) must exist and have dated sources. Without a research file, the agent stops and instructs running a researcher first.

---

## /skill-creator

> **Agent:** `artifact-author` | **Context:** fork | **Model invocation:** disabled

### When to Use

Use after having a `research_<Tech>_v<Version>.md` from any researcher and wanting to transform it into an operational SKILL.md for Claude Code.

**Trigger words:** "create a FastAPI skill", "generate SKILL.md for Redis", "compile research into skill", "transform research into skill".

### Prerequisites

- Research file must exist: `research_<TechName>_v<Version>.md`
- The file must contain a Source Bibliography with dated sources
- If the file does not exist → run `/researching-technical-frameworks` first

### Inputs

| Field | Required | Example |
|-------|:-----------:|---------|
| Path to the research file | ✅ | `StoryBeat/research_FastAPI_v0.115.md` |

### Call Example

```
/skill-creator StoryBeat/research_FastAPI_v0.115.md
```

The agent will automatically derive from the file:
- Skill name: `fastapi-async-api` (kebab-case, gerund preferred)
- Version: `0.115`
- Three-Tier sections: Mandatory_Patterns → ✅, Conditional_Patterns → ⚠️, Forbidden_Patterns → 🚫

### Internal Workflow (7 steps)

1. Applies integrated authoring standards from `skill-creator` (quality baseline)
2. Reads the research file from `$ARGUMENTS`
3. Maps research sections to skill structure
4. Applies frontmatter rules (name ≤ 64 chars, description with "Use when…")
5. Generates `SKILL.md` with body ≤ 500 lines
6. Creates 3 evaluation scenarios in blueprints
7. Self-verifies against quality checklist

### Output Produced

```
.claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/
├── SKILL.md
└── blueprints/
    └── evaluation-scenarios.md
```

**Structure of the generated `SKILL.md`:**
```yaml
---
name: fastapi-async-api
description: >-
  Implements FastAPI 0.115 async endpoints following official patterns.
  Use when building REST APIs with FastAPI, Pydantic v2, and async SQLAlchemy.
allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash
---
```

Body: Version Context, ✅ Always Do (with executable code), ⚠️ Ask First (with trade-off table), 🚫 Never Do (with inline alternative), Verification Loop, External Resources.

### Post-Generation Verification

```bash
wc -l .claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/SKILL.md
# Expected: ≤ 500

grep -c "### ✅\|### ⚠️\|### 🚫" .claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/SKILL.md
# Expected: 3

test -f .claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/blueprints/evaluation-scenarios.md && echo "OK" || echo "MISSING"

grep -nE "(C:\\\\|/Users/|/home/)" .claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/SKILL.md
# Expected: no output (no absolute paths)
```

### Next Steps

- Validate quality → `/skill-best-practices-validator .claude/skills/fastapi-async-api/`
- Check overall health → `/project-analysis-validator .claude/`

### Never Do

- Invoke without a research file — without a research base, the agent stops
- Skip creating `blueprints/evaluation-scenarios.md` — it is mandatory
- Place absolute or Windows-style paths in the generated SKILL.md
- Mix content from different versions in the same SKILL.md

## /agent-creator

> **Agent:** `artifact-author` | **Context:** fork | **Model invocation:** disabled

### When to Use

Use when adding a new subagent to `.claude/agents/`, or converting a hand-written agent
definition into the house standard. Fills the gap the factory used to have: a command existed
for creating skills and for compiling rules, none existed for creating agents.

### What Happens

1. Reads `blueprints/agent-decision-tree.md` and picks one of 3 shapes: standard (executes and
   writes, P0–P5), advisory (read-only, recommends only), or orchestrator (multi-domain or
   fans out via `Agent`).
2. Generates `.claude/agents/<domain-role>.md` from the matching template in `./assets/`.
3. Validates the result against `.claude/rules/agent-frontmatter.md` and confirms at least one
   skill routes to the new agent (an agent with no `agent: <name>` skill pointing at it is
   unreachable).

### Never Do

- Declare a tool the agent's own workflow never calls — least privilege, checked against the
  agent body, not assumed
- Skip the decision tree and pattern-match off an unrelated existing agent

## /methodologies-skill-generator

> **Agent:** `artifact-author` | **Context:** fork | **Model invocation:** disabled

### When to Use

Use when you want to create a skill for an **engineering or process methodology** (Scrum, SAFe, Kanban, BPM, DORA, Team Topologies) **without having a prior research file** — this command researches and generates the skill in a single pipeline.

**Trigger words:** "create a Scrum skill", "SAFe 6 skill", "Kanban methodology as skill", "generate DORA Metrics skill".

> **Difference from `/skill-creator`:** This one does research + generation in a single step (all-in-one). The `/skill-creator` only generates from an existing research file.

### Prerequisites

None — research and generation are done internally.

### Inputs

| Field | Required | Example |
|-------|:-----------:|---------|
| Methodology | ✅ | `Scrum`, `SAFe`, `Kanban`, `BPM`, `DORA` |
| Edition / version | ✅ | `Scrum Guide 2020`, `SAFe 6.0` |
| Engineering context | Optional | `SaaS product squad, 2-week sprint` |
| Official URL | Optional | `https://scrumguides.org/` |

### Call Example

```
/methodologies-skill-generator Scrum
```

The agent will ask:
```
Edition: Scrum Guide 2020
Context: 8-person product squad, 2-week sprints
```

### Internal Pipeline (5 phases)

1. **Classification:** identifies the methodology type and complexity
2. **Authoritative research:** WebSearch/WebFetch from official sources with version absolutism
3. **SKILL.md generation:** applies three-tier, correct YAML, blueprints
4. **Self-validation:** verifies quality checklist
5. **Output:** saves skill and confirms to the user

### Output Produced

```
.claude/skills/scrum-sprint-practices/
├── SKILL.md
└── blueprints/
    └── evaluation-scenarios.md
```

### Next Steps

- `/skill-best-practices-validator .claude/skills/scrum-sprint-practices/`

## /architecture-approaches-skill-generator

> **Agent:** `artifact-author` | **Context:** fork | **Model invocation:** disabled

### When to Use

Use when you want to create a skill for a **software architecture methodology or notation** (C4, DDD, TOGAF, ADR, UML, ArchiMate, Event-Driven) **without having a prior research file**.

**Trigger words:** "create a C4 Model skill", "DDD skill", "generate an ADR skill", "TOGAF 10 skill", "architecture notation as skill".

> **Difference from `/skill-creator`:** All-in-one pipeline (research + generates). Use `/skill-creator` if you already have a `research_<Methodology>.md` ready from `/architecture-methodology-researcher`.

### Prerequisites

None — research and generation are done internally.

### Inputs

| Field | Required | Example |
|-------|:-----------:|---------|
| Methodology / notation | ✅ | `C4 Model`, `DDD`, `TOGAF`, `ADR`, `UML 2.5` |
| Edition / version | ✅ | `C4 v4`, `TOGAF 10`, `UML 2.5` |
| Architecture context | Optional | `microservices, payments platform` |
| Official URL | Optional | `https://c4model.com/` |

### Call Example

```
/architecture-approaches-skill-generator C4 Model
```

The agent will ask:
```
Edition: v4 (2024)
Context: e-commerce platform with 15 services
Abstraction level: System Context + Container
```

### Research → Three-Tier Mapping

| Research Section | Skill Tier |
|-------------------|---------------|
| Mandatory patterns | ✅ Always Do |
| Architectural decisions | ⚠️ Ask First |
| Anti-patterns | 🚫 Never Do |

### Output Produced

```
.claude/skills/c4-model-architecture/
├── SKILL.md
└── blueprints/
    └── evaluation-scenarios.md
```

## /terraform-instructions-compiler

> **Agent:** `artifact-author` | **Context:** fork | **Model invocation:** disabled

### When to Use

Use after `/terraform-engineering-best-practices-researcher` to compile the research into scoped
rules/instructions files that a runtime automatically injects by file pattern — `.claude/rules/*.md`
(`paths:`) for Claude Code, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` (`applyTo:`) for Copilot,
selected by `TARGET_PLATFORM`. Both dialects come from the same generic templates and the same
5-phase engine (see the [rules-compiler](../../.claude/skills/rules-compiler/SKILL.md) note below).

**Trigger words:** "compile Terraform rules", "generate Terraform instructions", "create IaC rules", "compile Terraform for project".

> **Difference from `/skill-creator`:** Produces rules/instructions, not `SKILL.md`. Rules/instructions are automatically injected by file scope; skills are called explicitly. Use to define project standards, not generation capabilities.

### Prerequisites

- Research file must exist: `research_Terraform_Engineering_Best_Practices_v<Version>.md`
- Generated by `/terraform-engineering-best-practices-researcher`

### Inputs

| Field | Required | Example |
|-------|:-----------:|---------|
| Research file | ✅ | `StoryBeat/research_Terraform_Engineering_Best_Practices_v1.9.md` |
| Terraform Version | Derived from file | `1.9` |
| Cloud Provider | Derived from file | `AWS` |
| Project root | Optional | `.` (workspace root) |
| Target platform | Optional (default: `claude-code`) | `claude-code` → `.claude/rules/`, `copilot` → `.github/instructions/` |

### Call Example

```
/terraform-instructions-compiler StoryBeat/research_Terraform_Engineering_Best_Practices_v1.9.md
```

### Internal Pipeline (5 phases, from the generic engine)

This skill is a **domain compiler** — it supplies Terraform data (file matrix, pattern catalog,
interview questions) to the generic 5-phase engine in
[`rules-compiler`](../../.claude/skills/rules-compiler/SKILL.md), which any future
`<domain>-instructions-compiler` (e.g. Kubernetes, AWS) would also link into instead of forking:

1. **Load** the research file and the 3 generic templates (`TEMPLATE.STANDARDS.md`,
   `TEMPLATE.CONFIG.md`, `TEMPLATE.SKILLS.md`) from `rules-compiler/assets/`
2. **Interactive interview** (up to 16 questions): which aspects to include, project context
3. **Planning**: presents the file matrix and waits for approval
4. **Generation**: fills the templates with Terraform data, writes files per `TARGET_PLATFORM`
5. **Validation**: coverage matrix — 0 uncovered mandatory/forbidden patterns

### Output Produced

For `TARGET_PLATFORM: claude-code` (default):
```
.claude/rules/
├── terraform-project-config.md    ← backend setup, providers, versions
├── terraform-standards.md         ← naming, module structure, tags
└── terraform-skills.md            ← keywords → skills routing table
```
Each file has the correct `paths:` field, e.g. `terraform-standards` → `paths: ["**/*.tf", "**/modules/**"]`.

For `TARGET_PLATFORM: copilot`, the same content is written to `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`
with `applyTo:` instead of `paths:` — same templates, same interview, only the output dialect changes.

### Post-Generation Verification

```bash
ls .github/instructions/terraform-*.instructions.md
grep "applyTo:" .github/instructions/terraform-*.instructions.md
```

### Next Steps

- Validate instructions quality → `/instructions-best-practices-validator .github/instructions/`

---

## Agent Principles

**Progressive Disclosure** — SKILL.md stays below 500 lines. Extensive content goes into linked `blueprints/`.

**Mandatory Three-Tier** — no tier may be empty. Every ✅ has executable code. Every 🚫 has an inline alternative with impact.

**Valid frontmatter:**
- `name`: ≤ 64 chars, kebab-case, without reserved words (`anthropic`, `claude`)
- `description`: third person, includes "Use when…", ≤ 1536 chars
- Skills use `allowed-tools:`; agents use `tools:` — never swap them
